title: DVD-Quant: Data-free Video Diffusion Transformers Quantization
claim: Baseline methods collapse into artifacts under extreme low-bit quantization, while ours stays close to full-precision quality with higher scores.
layout: 3 columns by 3 rows of film strips; full-precision reference on top, dashed divider
description: A grid of film-strip frames comparing three methods: MinMax, ViiT-Q and DVD-Quant (orange, highlighted). The top row is a full-width BF16 reference strip showing a snowy mountain scene. A dashed line separates it from two rows labeled 'W4A *'. Each cell has a blue pill giving the activation bit-width (* = 8, 6 or 4) and a green pill giving average imaging quality. In the upper row, the baselines score about 60 and DVD-Quant scores 64.22 at 6 bits. In the lower row at 4 bits, MinMax is an unrecognizable black-and-orange blob (24.78), ViiT-Q is distorted (40.10), and DVD-Quant stays clean and bluish (61.82). The eye goes first to the corrupted MinMax frames, then to the orange DVD-Quant column.
caption: $\ours$ generates high-fidelity videos under both W4A6 (mixed-precision) and W4A4 settings, while baseline methods fail under low-bit activation quantization. $\ours$ remains effective even in such extreme scenarios.
abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have emerged as the state-of-the-art architecture for video generation, yet their computational and memory demands hinder practical deployment. While post-training quantization (PTQ) presents a promising approach to accelerate Video DiT models, existing methods suffer from two critical limitations: (1) dependence on computation-heavy and inflexible calibration procedures, and (2) considerable performance deterioration after quantization. To address these challenges, we propose DVD-Quant, a novel Data-free quantization framework for Video DiTs. Our approach integrates three key innovations: (1) Bounded-init Grid Refinement (BGR) and (2) Auto-scaling Rotated Quantization (ARQ) for calibration data-free quantization error reduction, as well as (3) $Î´$-Guided Bit Switching ($Î´$-GBS) for adaptive bit-width allocation. Extensive experiments across multiple video generation benchmarks demonstrate that DVD-Quant achieves an approximately 2$\times$ speedup over full-precision baselines on advanced DiT models while maintaining visual fidelity. Notably, DVD-Quant is the first to enable W4A4 PTQ for Video DiTs without compromising video quality. Code and models will be available at https://github.com/lhxcs/DVD-Quant.
